formMapping: Devfolio MCP authenticated. Current project, organizer fields, tracks and gallery read back through getMyHackathonProject.
problem: Facility operators accept monitoring equipment installed by independent contractors. Failed installations create disputed handovers, manual checks, and potential repeat visits. An installation photo does not establish that equipment meets the agreed checks.
solution: Remote acceptance testing for contractor-installed monitoring equipment. The operator defines the checks, reviews camera and device evidence, and receives an independent paid report before accepting the handover. The demonstrated installation fails placement, and its paid report explains the defect.
currentImplementation: Actual Seeker camera evidence returned REWORK for incorrect placement. An independent inspector reviewed that exact camera evidence, returned a useful FAIL report, and received 1 test USDM on Cardano Preprod. Escrow, result, withdrawal, and positive seller collection verified. A separate earlier paid REVIEW used synthetic input and remains labeled. An ESP32 signed 18-second diagnostic and 72 recorded optical symbols verified separately. No complete fresh work-order-bound optical commissioning capture or button test exists. Three genuine paid NVD requests settled. A mandatory source-gated Base Sepolia policy admitted a declared reference build and opened a work order before inspection. The four deployed tamper cases reject. A vulnerable reference build and the unsigned entry point also reject. The earlier five cases and mined rejection remain unchanged. Installed ESP32 firmware remains unproven. The application is deterministic and operator-driven. It does not run autonomous LLM reasoning. A read-only phone viewer presents saved real evidence offline after one load. The physical Seeker passed portrait rendering, offline reload, and all six saved-file hashes with browser networking disabled.

Measure marker placement. Signed contact and optical test protocols exist, but the physical commissioning sequence remains incomplete.

whySignedDataMatters: A forged or substituted vulnerability response can misstate software acceptance. The contract checks the configured Airnode, exact CVE request and source age. NVD signatures do not identify firmware installed on a physical device.
businessCase: Proposed customer: facility operators and installation integrators that accept contractor-installed monitoring equipment. Proposed model: a paid inspection per handover. Clear defect evidence supports correction before acceptance. Customer demand, pricing, fewer repeat visits, and cost savings remain unvalidated.

organizerFieldAnswers.name: The problem it solves
organizerFieldAnswers.value:
Facility operators need proof before accepting contractor-installed equipment. signoff combines camera measurements, signed device evidence and a paid inspection. Our real camera check found incorrect placement. The inspector returned FAIL and received 1 test USDM on Cardano Preprod. Installation acceptance stayed blocked.

Proposed customer: facility operators and monitoring integrators managing handovers across sites. Proposed model: paid inspection per handover. Demand and pricing remain unvalidated.

Sokosumi/Masumi provides escrow, result delivery and seller withdrawal. API3 authenticates NVD data before our deployed Base Sepolia contract opens a software-gated work order. Original fresh data caused mined admission for a declared reference build. Edited, stale, different-request and wrong-key data reject. Removing API3 prevents admission.

The LED diagnostic, camera preview, paid attempt and software admission are separate real runs. They do not prove complete physical installation. Full optical/contact tests and installed-firmware provenance remain unfinished. Source signatures do not establish physical truth. We wanted authenticated manufacturer provenance tied to the board, which this source does not provide. The workflow is deterministic and operator-driven.

Real operation needs enrolled devices, reviewed wiring, calibration, reliable network/RPC access and configured inspector credentials.

organizerFieldAnswers.name: Challenges we ran into
organizerFieldAnswers.value:
Exact camera evidence, signed receipts, report and payment bindings required immutable approvals, preserved original bytes, durable claims, and restart/concurrency tests.

The older contract rejected a failed inspection without establishing source dependence. We added mandatory authenticated NVD approval before work-order opening. The new contract produced an actual mined admission. Four tamper inputs reject, as do a vulnerable build and unsigned opening.

Real camera placement still fails. We preserved REWORK and the paid FAIL rather than substituting fixtures for missing evidence. The earlier paid synthetic REVIEW remains separate. Complete physical tests and installed-firmware provenance remain unfinished.

Historical RPC reads intermittently fail. Those failures are inconclusive, never contract rejection. Original mined proof and historical context remain preserved.
